messages:
olivia: heads-up — customer `acme` escalated p95 for the text-gen route at ~03:00 UTC. Our p95 panel shows ~120ms -> ~450ms, but the latency histogram panel doesn't show the same shift. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd123/latency

sre-bot: :rotating_light: alert fired: latency.p95.route=text-gen > 3x baseline for 15m (alert id: A-9832)

ashwin: pulling prometheus. can you paste exact route label? also, which dashboard panel queries are we looking at?

olivia: route=\"text-gen.v1\" — panel A uses: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))`
panel B is a histogram heatmap over `redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket` (same metric)

ashwin: running quick checks — first, list unique `le` values by cluster:
```
label_values(sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cluster), le)
```
returns: us-west: [0.01,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,1,2.5,5], eu-central: [0.01,0.049999999,0.09999999,0.25,0.5,1,2.5,5]

kai: that mismatch is the smoking gun — histogram_quantile requires identical bucket boundaries across the aggregated series. if eu has slightly different `le` floats, summing buckets before histogram_quantile produces garbage. the heatmap panel is showing raw buckets so it looked \"flat\" because bucket indexing differs per-cluster.

maria: correct — we rolled the exporter v0.8 -> v0.9 in eu yesterday which bumped the default bucket set (and floating precision). the eu exporter emitted slightly different floating `le` values. we also enabled our rollup recording rule that sums buckets across clusters: `sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)` — that combined mismatch caused histogram_quantile to compute wrong percentiles.

ashwin: reproducer quick note:
1) take two series with different `le` lists\2) do `sum by (le) (rate(...))` -> you'll see inconsistent counts lined up to non-matching boundaries
3) `histogram_quantile(0.95, ...)` over that output can under/over-estimate p95 depending on where mismatches land

olivia: immediate mitigations we can do now? customer is on-calls waiting.

kai: short-term: change grafana panel to compute percentiles per-cluster (i.e. do histogram_quantile per cluster then combine) — like:
```
max( histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cluster, route)) ) by (route)
```
That avoids summing mismatched buckets. show per-cluster lines for troubleshooting.

maria: i can push a hotfix to the dashboard now to switch to per-cluster quantiles and add a note on the panel about \"do not sum buckets across exporters\". that's low risk.

ashwin: medium-term: align bucket boundaries across exporters and add a unit test in exporter CI that ensures `label_values(..., le)` lists match canonical set. also add a recording rule that computes `redwood_request_duration_p95{cluster}` using histogram_quantile at ingestion time so graphs can read a single scalar. example recording rule:
```
- record: request_duration_seconds_p95
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cluster, route))
```

olivia: sounds good. can we also add a fallback panel to use t-digest based precomputed percentiles (we ship t-digest in telemetry) so we have a secondary SLI?

maria: eu rollback scheduled — i'm reverting exporter in eu to v0.8 in the next 15m. i'll also open a PR to standardize buckets and add the CI gate.

kai: i'll update the runbook: note about never summing histogram_bucket across heterogeneous exporters; step-by-step to validate `le` sets; how to create per-cluster recording rules.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-042 (owner: maria) — paging stakeholders: @observability-team, @platform-eng

olivia: thanks team — customer notified that we're working it. maria, please post the follow-up in #incidents/postmortems and add the timeline+root-cause. mark this thread for handoff to next oncall. :thumbsup:
